reviews.reason: The wp_ajax_backwpup_debug_info closure at inc/class-admin.php:281-291 has no current_user_can() or check_ajax_referer() guard before calling BackWPup_Page_Settings::get_information() and echoing the results. The wp_ajax_ prefix requires WordPress login but imposes no capability filter, so any authenticated user including a plain subscriber with no BackWPup roles can obtain the full debug report containing DOCUMENT_ROOT, temp/log folder absolute paths, PHP user, server self-connect response, and loaded PHP extensions. The guard_contradiction issue in the gate is a false positive: there genuinely is no guard. The finding is consistent.
missing_evidence: Whether the admin page that embeds the debug-info link requires backwpup_settings — the AJAX action itself is callable without it.
Whether get_information() makes outbound HTTP requests (self-connect check) that could be observable as SSRF side effects.

Step 4: Repeat with a backwpup_check role user to confirm same disclosure.
Step 5: Confirm the hook fires without any _wpnonce parameter.

reviews.reason: The shared save_post_form() handler at inc/class-admin.php:838-852 checks check_admin_referer(._page) and current_user_can(backwpup) — not backwpup_jobs_edit. When onboarding===1, it delegates to BackWPup_Page_Onboarding::save_post_form() at line 892-895 without any secondary capability check. The backwpup_check role (backwpup=true, backwpup_jobs_edit=false) can access the onboarding submenu (inc/class-admin.php:658-667 requires only backwpup_backups) and thus obtain the backwpup_page nonce. The BAC violation is that the onboarding branch bypasses the job-edit check that all other job-mutating branches enforce.
